subject: Initial scoping: Dedicated GPU suitability & autoscale expectations
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: David Liu <david.liu@novacorp.ai>, Procurement <procurement@novacorp.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Initial scoping: Dedicated GPU suitability & autoscale expectations

Hi David —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call so we have alignment and a clear set of next steps. If anything below looks off or missing, please flag it and I’ll update.

High-level goals
- Move inference for NovaSearch (semantic search + generative answers) off noisy shared endpoints and onto a predictable Dedicated pool.
- Reduce tail latency for low-latency queries (95th pct target <= 120ms for short queries).
- Control unit economics during daytime peak and provide safe burst capacity for spikes.

Primary pain points you shared
- Unpredictable latency from current multi-tenant API, especially during business-hours spikes.
- Request volume variability: big marketing campaigns and batch re-ranks cause short bursts.
- Data isolation requirement for certain customers (must run in a private VPC with customer-managed keys).

Current stack / baseline
- Model: open Llama-2-13B fine-tuned for ranking + generation.
- Serving today: third-party hosted endpoint (per-request) with observed 95th pct = 300-600ms under load.
- Typical traffic: baseline 120 TPS (inference tokens ~45 tokens/req), peak bursts up to ~900 TPS for ~5–20 minute windows during campaigns.

Success criteria for Dedicated fit
- Predictable steady-state throughput: support 120 TPS with 95th <= 120ms.
- Burst behavior: support spikes to 900 TPS for up to 20 minutes with graceful degradation beyond burst budget.
- Isolation: Dedicated pool must be in NovaCorp VPC + KMS integration.
- Cost target: reduce per-token serving cost by at least 25% vs current provider over a 30-day window (goal metric).

Preliminary sizing notes (requesting your confirmation)
- Warm pool baseline suggestion: 2 x A100-like GPUs for baseline traffic (assumes quantized model, batching ~1–4).
- Burst sizing: policy to allow temporary burst up to 6 GPUs (4x baseline) with autoscale cooldown 10–15 min and a concurrency cap to protect backend.
- KV/prefix cache: recommend enabling to optimize repeat prefix costs for re-rank-heavy requests.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Could you confirm the estimated average tokens per request and % of requests that are re-rank vs full generation? (I have 45 tokens/req and ~30% re-rank from today’s call.)
2) Can procurement share any billing/contract constraints (PO cadence, standard SOW terms, security addenda)?
3) If you’re happy with the approach above, we’ll schedule a technical deep-dive with Ben (SE) and Laura (AM) to nail down pool sizing, autoscale knobs, and pilot timeline.

Attachments: I attached a short capacity sizing template (capacity-sizing-template.xlsx) — please fill the baseline/peak columns and return.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with proposed times for the technical deep-dive.

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0172

From: David Liu <david.liu@novacorp.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@novacorp.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial scoping: Dedicated GPU suitability & autoscale expectations

Irene —

Thanks for the tidy summary. Confirming the numbers from our end:
- Avg tokens/request: 42 (close to your 45).
- Re-rank vs full gen: ~33% re-rank.
- Typical concurrency per user session: 3–5 simultaneous small queries.
- Peak spike we saw last quarter: ~880 TPS sustained for ~12 minutes (campaign-driven).

Security: NovaCorp requires VPC peering and KMS integration for customer PII workloads; SOC 2 attestation is required for any production pilot. I’ve attached our procurement questionnaire — procurement@novacorp.ai will coordinate.

Pilot timeline: we’re targeting a pilot in mid-September if we can lock scope and compliance.

Questions:
1) For the burst proposal, what’s the expected failover behavior if burst capacity is exhausted? Do you have an automatic fallback to a cheaper, lower-capacity pool or spill to shared endpoints?
2) Can we get an estimate of per-hour cost at baseline vs at full-burst? Even a rough delta helps our finance folks.

Happy to jump on the deep-dive next week if Ben/Laura are available.

—David
David Liu
Director, Platform Engineering | NovaCorp
david.liu@novacorp.ai

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: David Liu <david.liu@novacorp.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@novacorp.ai>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial scoping: Dedicated GPU suitability & autoscale expectations

Thanks David — helpful detail. Quick answers inline and proposed next steps below.

Questions from your note
1) Fallback behavior: Redwood has configurable fallback policies. Recommended default for this pilot:
   - If Dedicated burst budget is exhausted, traffic spills to a pre-configured lower-cost shared fallback model with rate-limiting and degraded latency guarantees (we’ll surface metrics and offer rate-limit and token caps to avoid surprises).
   - We can optionally prioritize certain customer routes to avoid impacting highest-value traffic.

2) Rough cost estimate: baseline (2 GPUs, warm) ~ $X/hour; full burst (6 GPUs) ~ ~3x baseline/hour. Those are very coarse until we lock batch sizes and quantization. We’ll supply a model-level estimate in the technical deep-dive.

Proposed pilot scope & timeline
- Pilot window: 2 weeks isolated environment in NovaCorp VPC (non-production subset of traffic).
- Objectives: validate 120 TPS steady-state; validate 900 TPS short bursts up to 20 min with acceptable degradation profile; verify KMS + VPC integration and logging.
- Acceptance criteria: 95th < 120ms for baseline and documented degradation curve for burst events.

Next steps
1) Please return the attached capacity-sizing-sheet with any corrected numbers (thanks for the questionnaire — procurement team can send any legal templates).
2) Ben to run technical deep-dive to produce a firm GPU/hour estimate and confirm autoscale knobs.
3) We’ll spin up a pilot pre-prod pool + small canary traffic to validate end-to-end before the full pilot.

Scheduling: Ben and Laura are available for a 60-min deep-dive on Wed 2026-08-05 at 10:00am PT or Thu 2026-08-06 at 11:30am PT. Which works for you and your team?

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-fit-checklist.pdf (high-level checklist we use for pilots).

Thanks — looping Ben to propose the technical agenda.

Best,
Irene

David / team —

Great to meet you (virtually) — thanks for the clear notes, Irene. Wed 08/05 10:00am PT works; I’ve attached a short technical agenda below and a calendar invite link in case that helps.

Proposed technical agenda (60m)
- 00:00–05:00: Introductions & objectives (Irene / Laura)
- 05:00–25:00: Current traffic profile & model details (David)
- 25:00–45:00: Redwood runtime/pool behavior: warm pool sizing, autoscale policy, KV cache, quantization options (Ben)
- 45:00–55:00: Failure modes & fallback policies (Ben)
- 55:00–60:00: Next steps & pilot kickoff (all)

Quick technical notes to prep
- Warm pool recommendation: min_pool = 2 GPUs. We’ll provision enough instances so batching and KV cache warm-up meets your latency targets.
- Burst policy suggestion: allow up to x3 baseline GPUs for 10–20 minutes with an autoscale cooldown of 10 minutes; if exceeded, apply graceful degradation and redirect lower-priority routes to fallback shared pool.
- Observability: we’ll instrument per-route token/cost breakdown and a latency heatmap during pilot.

Calendar: https://meet.example/irene-ben-novacorp-0805 (please use this link; invite will show in your calendar shortly).

Ben
